key_points.text: Thinking concurrently means working out which parts of a problem can be done at the same time and which depend on the results of others (and so must wait).
Benefits: more tasks done in a given time, less time spent waiting (for example, for input or a file), and better use of the processor and of multiple cores.

Trade-offs: it is harder to design, program and debug; tasks that depend on each other can't run at the same time; and tasks sharing data must be coordinated so they don't interfere, which adds overhead.
For a scenario, be ready to say how concurrent processing could be applied to a specific program, why it would help, and what problems might arise.

dont_confuse.text: Concurrent vs parallel: concurrent tasks overlap in time (possibly by switching on one processor); parallel tasks run at the same instant on separate processors or cores.
